decisive_items: CD20+, Pax5+, BcL-2+, BcL-6+, CD10−, mum-1+, Cmyc+ (40%)
response.rationale: Splenic biopsy shows a mature B-cell neoplasm with CD20/Pax5 positivity, Bcl-6/MUM1 expression, C-myc 40%, and Ki67 80%, diagnostic of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. HIV and low CD4 provide relevant context but the specific pathologic phenotype makes DLBCL the best diagnosis; HIV-associated lymphoma is a reasonable broader alternative.

rejected.why: Descriptive splenomegaly/lymphoproliferative disorder, not a specific diagnosis and less informative than the biopsy-proven DLBCL phenotype.
Castleman disease can cause splenomegaly and adenopathy, but the MUM1+, C-myc+, Ki67 80% B-cell immunophenotype favors an aggressive lymphoma rather than Castleman disease.
Tuberculosis is historically relevant, but the progressive splenic lesions, hypermetabolic bone foci, and B-cell IHC are not explained by tuberculosis and the splenic biopsy confirms lymphoma.
